System Location

III. Thien Dam

items.x: Rihand dam is in Uttar Pradesh (Sonbhadra), Farakka Barrage in West Bengal and Thein (Ranjit Sagar) dam on the Ravi in Punjab. Moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: Through which Indian state does river 'Chambal' flow initially before entering another state?
items.x: The Chambal rises near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh and then flows into Rajasthan.

items.s: Naimisaranya was located on the banks of which river?
items.x: Naimisaranya (Nimsar, Sitapur district, UP) lies on the left bank of the Gomati (Gomti), a plains-fed Ganga tributary. It is not on the Ganga, Yamuna or Narmada.

items.s: Which of the following is not a tributary of the river Brahmaputra?
items.x: The Luni is an inland river of Rajasthan lost in the Rann of Kutch. The Teesta, Manas and Dihang (the Brahmaputra's name in Arunachal) belong to the Brahmaputra system.

items.s: Which one of the following rivers is NOT the part of Indian Ganga river basin?
items.x: The Jonk is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi, so it is not in the Ganga basin. The Punpun (Bihar), Ajoy and Jalangi (West Bengal) belong to the Ganga system.

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: In which of the following rivers is the Majuli River Island situated?
items.x: Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.

items.s: The changing course of the river Brahmaputra and its tributaries led to the formation of ____ island.
items.x: The shifting channels of the Brahmaputra and its tributaries (Subansiri, Kherkutia Xuti) formed Majuli island.

items.src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer, Assistant Public Relation
items.s: Majuli Island is the largest river island in India. In which state is this island located?
items.x: Majuli is in Assam, in the Brahmaputra.

items.s: Majuli (Assam), the largest riverine island in the world is the best example of good ______ crops after the annual floods in Brahmaputra.
items.x: The silt laid down by the Brahmaputra's annual floods makes Majuli fertile for paddy, its main crop.

items.s: The Bhagirathi river originates from –
items.x: The Bhagirathi emerges at Gomukh, the snout of the Gangotri glacier, about 18 km from Gangotri town.

items.s: On which river is the world's largest river island?
items.x: Majuli in the Brahmaputra (Assam) is described as the largest riverine island in the world.

items.s: Name the river which flows between Kedarnath and Rudra prayag ?
items.x: The Mandakini rises at Chorabari Taal near Kedarnath and joins the Alaknanda at Rudraprayag.

items.s: Which one of the following is not located along the Mandakini river ?
items.x: Gaurikund, Rambara and Guptakashi are on the Mandakini; Govindghat lies at the Alaknanda–Lakshman Ganga confluence.

items.s: Which of the following rivers does not fall into river Yamuna ?
items.x: The Son joins the Ganga directly near Patna; the Ken, Betwa and Chambal join the Yamuna.

items.s: On which river is Mata Tila Dam situated?
items.x: The Matatila dam is on the Betwa in Lalitpur district, UP.

items.s: With which drainage system or main river is Mandakini associated ?
items.x: The Mandakini belongs to the Alaknanda system, joining it at Rudraprayag.

items.s: Eastern Dhauliganga (Poorvi Dhauliganga) is a tributary of :
items.x: The Eastern (Poorvi) Dhauliganga rises near the Indo-Tibet border in Pithoragarh and joins the Kali (Sharda in the plains) at Tawaghat; the Western Dhauliganga joins the Alaknanda at Vishnuprayag, which is the tempting wrong option.

items.s: 'Doodh-Ganga' river is located in –
items.x: The Doodh Ganga is a Jhelum tributary that rises in the Pir Panjal and flows through Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir; no river of that name is notable in West Bengal (the printed key). A Dudhganga also exists in Maharashtra–Karnataka (Krishna system), but that state is not offered.

items.s: Hizla fair of Dumka in Santhal Pargana is celebrated on the bank of which of the following rivers?
items.x: The Hijla (Hizla) fair of Dumka, Santhal Pargana, is held on the bank of the Mayurakshi river every spring.

items.s: Ujjain is located –
o: On the bank of River Chambal
On the bank of River Kshipra
On the bank of River Godavari
On the bank of River Narmada
items.x: Ujjain (Simhastha Kumbh) is on the Kshipra (Shipra), a tributary of the Chambal; it is not on the Chambal, Godavari or Narmada.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
items.s: The Indian rivers are divided into... major groups.
items.x: Indian rivers are grouped into two major systems: the Himalayan and the Peninsular rivers. Three, five or six groups are not the standard division.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
items.s: The Gandak river that rises in the Nepal Himalayas enters the Ganga plain in the Indian state of
items.x: The Gandak rises in the Nepal Himalayas and enters the Ganga plain in Bihar (it forms part of the UP–Bihar border), joining the Ganga near Patna.

items.src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
items.s: The largest estuary in India in terms of area is at the mouth of the river?
items.x: The Hooghly estuary (Ganga delta, West Bengal) is India's largest estuary by area. Narmada and Tapti have smaller west-coast estuaries; the Mahanadi forms a delta.

items.s: In Tibet, the ____ is known as 'Langchen Khambab'.
items.x: In Tibet the Satluj is called Langchen Khambab ('elephant mouth'); the Indus is Singi Khamban.

items.s: Which of the following is an example of an antecedent river?
items.x: Antecedent rivers such as the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra rise in the Trans-Himalaya and cut gorges as ranges rise.

items.s: Majuli is which of the following?
o: A delta of the Godavari on the eastern coast
A river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam
A waterfall on the Cauvery in Karnataka
A tributary of the Krishna in Telangana
items.x: Majuli is a large river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.

items.s:
Assertion (A): The Bist Doab lies between the Beas and the Sutlej.
Reason (R): The Chaj Doab lies between the Ravi and the Chenab.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
items.x: Bist lies between the Beas and Sutlej, but the Chaj lies between the Chenab and Jhelum; the Ravi-Chenab doab is the Rechna.

items.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which of the following rivers is allocated to India?
items.x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej go to India; the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab mainly to Pakistan.

items.s: Where does the Bhagirathi River rise?
items.x: The Bhagirathi rises at Gomukh, at the Gangotri glacier.

items.s: The westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga is the:
items.x: The Yamuna is the westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga; the Chambal and Betwa join it first.

items.s: In May 2026, how did India respond to the Court of Arbitration's award under the Indus Waters Treaty?
o: It referred the award to the World Bank
It challenged the award at the ICJ
It rejected the award as 'null and void'
items.x: India rejected the award as 'null and void'; it has held the treaty in abeyance since 2025.

items.s: The Gandak is regarded as India's second-largest habitat for gharials after which river?
items.x: The Gandak is India's second-largest gharial habitat, after the Chambal.

items.s: Which is the largest river island of India?
items.x: Majuli in Assam is the largest river island.

items.s:
Consider the following statements about the Panchprayag confluences:
1. Karnaprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini.
2. Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Rudraprayag is the Alaknanda–Mandakini confluence; Karnaprayag is the Alaknanda–Pindar confluence.

items.s: Between which rivers does the Rechna Doab lie?
items.x: Rechna = Ravi–Chenab; Bist = Beas–Sutlej; Chaj = Chenab–Jhelum.

items.s: Where does the Mandakini rise?
items.x: The Mandakini rises at Chorabari Taal and joins the Alaknanda at Rudraprayag.

items.s: Majuli was the first river island of India to be made what?
items.x: Majuli on the Brahmaputra is the first river island to become a district.

items.s: The Kshipra is a tributary of which river?
items.x: The Chambal's tributaries include the Kali Sindh, Parvati and Kshipra.

items.s: Which of the following is the correct order of the left-bank tributaries of the Ganga from west to east?
items.x: From west to east the left-bank tributaries are Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda.

items.s: Wular Lake is situated on which river and between which ranges?
o: Kaveri; Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats
items.x: Wular is a freshwater lake on the Jhelum, situated between the Pir Panjal and Zaskar ranges.

items.s: The Baglihar dam is on which river?
items.x: Baglihar is on the Chenab; Pandoh is on the Beas.

items.s: Prayagraj is at the confluence of the Ganga and which river?
items.x: Prayagraj lies at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence; Varanasi, Patna and Bhagalpur are on the Ganga.

items.s: On which river is Lucknow situated?
items.x: Lucknow is on the Gomati; Surat is on the Tapi and Jabalpur on the Narmada.

items.src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III (Endowment) Paper-I Genera
items.s: With which national code is the area between the Godavari river basin and the Mahanadi river basin encompassing the eastern ghats designated?
items.x: The printed key F is kept: the question refers to a national basin coding of the east-flowing rivers between the Mahanadi and the Godavari. The code could not be found in the library or online, so the owner should check it.

items.s: The longest river of South India is based in Andhra Pradesh. What is the name of this river?
items.x: The Godavari (~1,465 km, 'Dakshin Ganga') is the longest river of South (Peninsular) India and ends in Andhra Pradesh; the Krishna (~1,400 km) is second.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
items.s: Which is the longest River of Peninsular India?
items.x: The Godavari (about 1,465 km, rising at Trimbakeshwar) is the longest river of Peninsular India, hence 'Dakshin Ganga'. Moved to Peninsular drainage.

items.src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
items.s:

R: They are born in Sahyadri Range
o: A and R are correct but R does not explain A
A is correct but R is wrong
A & r are Correct and R explains A
a is wrong but R is Correct
items.x: Most Deccan rivers flow west to east because the plateau tilts east; they do rise in the Sahyadri, but that alone does not explain the eastward flow. Moved (peninsular drainage).

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: Which of the following rivers flow into the Arabian Sea?
items.x: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). Off-topic (drainage), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forests General Studies & Men
items.s: From the given pairs, choose the correctly matched pair.
items.x: Garbled single-answer question: Indus - Arabian Sea, Mahanadi - Bay of Bengal and Thamirabarani - Gulf of Mannar are all correct, and Vaigai ends in Palk Bay (an arm of the Bay of Bengal), so no single pair can be chosen. Off-topic (drainage), moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: Which among the following Indian Rivers flows westwards and falls into Arabian Sea?
items.x: The Tapi (Tapti) flows west through a rift valley into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea). Off-topic, moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s:

Waterfall:

B. Kunchikal Falls
C. Dudhsagar Waterfalls
D. Barehipani Falls
Location (State): (i) Meghalaya (ii) Karnataka (iii) Goa (iv) Odisha
items.x: Nohkalikai – Meghalaya, Kunchikal – Karnataka, Dudhsagar – Goa, Barehipani – Odisha. Moved to drainage.

items.s: The river Bharathapuzha flows mainly in which state?
items.x: The Bharathapuzha (Nila), Kerala's second-longest river, rises in the Anamalai hills and flows west mainly through Kerala.

items.s: The Sabarmati river originates at the
items.x: The Sabarmati rises in the Aravalli hills (Udaipur district, Rajasthan) and flows into the Gulf of Khambhat.

items.s: How much of drainage area in the Indian drainage system is oriented towards the Bay of Bengal?
items.x: About 77% of India's drainage area is oriented towards the Bay of Bengal and about 23% towards the Arabian Sea. Off-topic (Indian drainage), moved.

items.s: In which state of India does the river Luni originate?
items.x: The Luni rises in the Aravalli range near Ajmer (Pushkar valley) in Rajasthan and ends in the Rann of Kachchh. Nagaland, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu are wrong.

items.s:
Arrange the following states in descending order in sharing the volume of Cauvery river water

a. Karnataka
b. Tamilnadu
c. Kerala
d. Pondichery
items.x: Under the Cauvery award TN gets the largest share, then Karnataka, Kerala and Puducherry (b, a, c, d).

items.s: Jog Waterfall, is located in the State of
items.x: Jog Falls, on the Sharavathi river, is in Shimoga district, Karnataka.

items.s: Where is the Kaliasot Dam located?
items.x: Kaliasot Dam is on the Kaliasot river in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.

items.s: From the following states, which one usually witnesses the blossom shower?
items.x: Blossom showers are pre-monsoon showers of Kerala (and Karnataka) that make coffee flowers blossom.

items.s: Which one of the following is the driest place?
items.x: Leh (Ladakh), a cold desert in the rain shadow of the Himalayas, gets under 10 cm of rain a year, far less than Mumbai, Delhi or Bengaluru. Moved to India's rainfall distribution.

items.src: Technical Assistant (Geophysics), Technical Assistants in AP
items.s: Average annual rain fall data of India over the years from 1901 indicates that, the average annual rain fall is in the range of?
items.x: India's long-period average annual rainfall since 1901 is about 1,100–1,200 mm (IMD LPA ~1,160 mm), so 1,100 mm is the nearest option.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: According to ISFR 2017, which State has shown highest increase in water bodies within forest area?
items.x: ISFR 2017 recorded the largest increase in water bodies inside forests in Maharashtra, followed by Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. Moved (ISFR).

items.src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
items.s:
Match the given mangrove forests of India with their respective state location and select the correct answer from the codes.
Name of Mangrove Forest:
A. Sundarbans
B. Pichavaram Mangroves
C. Bhitarkanika Mangroves
D. Baratang Mangroves
State: (i) West Bengal (ii) Odisha (iii) Andamans (iv) Tamil Nadu
items.x: Sundarbans – West Bengal, Pichavaram – Tamil Nadu, Bhitarkanika – Odisha, Baratang – Andamans. Moved to vegetation.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s:
Match column A with column B
Column A:
i. Recalcitrant seed
ii. Orthodox seed
iii. Vivipary
iv. Stump planting
Column B:

a. Vachellia nilotica

b. Shorea robusta

c. Tectona grandis

d. Rhizophora mucronata
items.x: Recalcitrant seed – sal (Shorea robusta), orthodox – babul (Vachellia nilotica), vivipary – Rhizophora mucronata, stump planting – teak (Tectona grandis). Off-topic, moved.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
items.s: The upper limit of tree growth in mountains or high latitudes is called as
items.x: The timber line (tree line) is the upper altitude (or high latitude) limit beyond which trees cannot grow. Off-topic (vegetation), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Timbers are broadly classified into two main groups based on their macrostructure. What are these groups?
items.x: By macrostructure timbers are classed as hardwood (broad-leaved, angiosperms) and softwood (conifers). Off-topic (forestry), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The practice of logging trees in forest areas that have been damaged by wildlife is called
items.x: Salvage logging is the removal of trees from forest damaged by fire, wind, disease or insects, to recover their timber value.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: On which of the following days is 'International Day of Forests' observed?
items.x: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 21 March the International Day of Forests (from 2013). 22 March is World Water Day and 22 April Earth Day.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which of the following is NOT a traditional logging tool?
items.x: A chainsaw is a modern powered machine; hand saw, axe, wedges and mauls are the traditional hand tools of logging. (Off-topic forestry question, moved.)

items.src: APPSC AE (Subordinate Services) Mains General Studies & Ment
items.s: Which is the National Tree of India?
items.x: The Banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is the National Tree of India; the Peepal, Neem and Mango are not. Off-topic, moved.

items.s: Acacia, Cacti, Khejra and Palas are the main plant species of the
items.x: Acacia, cacti, khejra and palas are thorn and scrub species of the dry north-west (Indus-Thar region of Punjab, Rajasthan and Sindh). Malabar is wet evergreen and Andaman tropical evergreen. Off-topic geography, moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which one is a traditional method of firefighting in forests?
items.x: Counter fire (back-firing – deliberately burning a strip ahead of the fire) is the traditional method of fighting forest fires; alert systems, mobile squads and communication devices are modern aids.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s:
Arrange the following States of India in ascending order of their forest-area and select the correct answer from the code given below:

a. Andhra Pradesh
b. Tamil Nadu
c. Odisha
d. Karnataka
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (b, a, d, c); it is added as option 5.
ISFR 2021 forest cover: Tamil Nadu 26,419 sq km < Andhra Pradesh 29,784 < Karnataka about 38,700 < Odisha 52,156, so the ascending order is b, a, d, c. The printed key (a, b, d, c) wrongly puts AP below Tamil Nadu; AP has had more forest than TN in every ISFR since bifurcation.

items.s: More than 90% of area of this Union Territory is covered by forests.
items.x: Lakshadweep has the highest forest cover by share of area: 91.33% (ISFR 2023), ahead of Andaman & Nicobar (81.62%).

items.src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
items.s: In which month Forest Festival is celebrated in our country?
items.x: Van Mahotsav, India's forest festival, is celebrated in the first week of July (started by K.M. Munshi in 1950).

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Systematic collection of data and forest information for assessment or analysis is referred to as
items.x: Systematic collection of forest data for assessment is a forest inventory. (Off-topic: moved to forests.)

items.s: What percentage of the country should be covered with forests in order to maintain the ecological balance?
items.x: The National Forest Policy 1988 aims at one-third (33%) of the area under forest or tree cover for ecological balance (60% in hills). (Moved to the forest-cover row.)

items.s: Degraded zone includes the area with heavy soil erosion
items.x: Acacia modesta, Capparis aphylla and Salvadora oleoides are all hardy dry-thorn species that survive on degraded, heavily eroded land in north-west India, so 'all of the above' is the answer.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
items.s: What percentage of the world's forests are made up of plantations?
items.x: FAO's Global Forest Resources Assessment 2020 puts plantation forests at about 3% of the world's forests (planted forests as a whole about 7%). Off-topic (world forests), moved.

items.s: As per the Economic Survey of India 2021-2022, forests covered 24 per cent of India's total geographical area accounting for .......... percent of the world's total forest area in 2020.
items.x: The Economic Survey 2021-22 says India's forests cover 24% of its geographical area and form about 2% of the world's forest area (2020). Off-topic (India forests), moved.

items.s: A Crown fire is very dangerous for a
items.x: A crown fire runs through the tree canopy and is most destructive in coniferous forests, whose resinous needles burn readily. Grassland and scrub fires are surface fires.

items.s: In which state of India, the per capita forest area is high?
items.x: With small populations and large forests, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have a high per capita forest area (about 1.8 ha), more than Mizoram, Himachal Pradesh or AP. Off-topic (India forests), moved.

items.s: Mangrove (Tidal Forests) vegetation in India is mostly found in –
items.x: India's largest mangrove (tidal) forests are in the Sundarbans of the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta, West Bengal. Off-topic (India vegetation), moved.

items.s: Which of the following woods is used for manufacturing Katha?
items.x: Katha (catechu) is obtained from the heartwood of Khair (Acacia catechu). Off-topic (India vegetation), moved.

items.s: The Wood of which tree is used for catechu production?
items.x: Catechu is obtained from the wood of the Khair tree (Acacia catechu). Off-topic (India vegetation), moved.

items.s: The state having lowest area under forest

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Which method of wood transport involves tying several logs together to move them as a single structure?
items.x: Rafting ties several logs together into a raft that floats downstream as one unit. Floating moves logs loose, one by one, and rope-ways and tramways are overland methods.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: Bhitarkanika in Odisha is a
items.x: Bhitarkanika in Odisha is a mangrove forest (national park and Ramsar site), known for saltwater crocodiles.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: Why is understanding wood anatomy essential for efficient use?
o: It helps identify aesthetically pleasing wood grains
It reveals the optimal methods for processing and utilization
It allows for accurate prediction of market trends
It helps trace the origins and history of specific wood pieces
items.x: Wood anatomy (cell structure, grain, density, pores) tells how a timber will behave when sawn, seasoned, preserved, glued or pulped, so it guides the best processing and end use; it does not predict markets or trace a piece's history.

items.src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
items.s: What is the scientific name of Sandalwood?
items.x: Sandalwood is Santalum album; Swertia chirata is chirayita, Cedrus deodara is deodar and Tectona grandis is teak.

items.s: Of which forest type is Sundari the characteristic tree?
items.x: Sundari is the typical tree of tidal (littoral) forests.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Himalayan forests?
o: Alpine forests occur at about 3,000–4,900 m
The coniferous belt below is the reason alpine forests occur higher up
Coniferous forests occur on the slopes at about 1,500–3,000 m
Alpine forests lie above the coniferous belt
items.x: Both altitude facts are true, but the coniferous belt at lower altitude does not explain why alpine forests occur higher up.

items.s: From which tree is catechu obtained?
items.x: Catechu comes from the wood of the Khair tree (Acacia catechu) of dry deciduous forests.

items.s: In which hills are Shola forests found?
items.x: Shola forests occur in the Nilgiri, Anamalai and Palani hills.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
items.s: In which of the following States is Simlipal bio reserve located?
items.x: Simlipal (Similipal) biosphere reserve is in Mayurbhanj district of Orissa (Odisha); it is also a tiger reserve and part of the Mayurbhanj elephant reserve.

items.x: Nagarhole (Kabini), Sathyamangalam (Moyar–Bhavani) and Wayanad (Kabini) lie in the Cauvery basin; Papikonda is on the Godavari. So A, C and D only. Off-topic (India protected areas), moved.

items.s: Where is Bandipur National Park situated?
items.x: Bandipur National Park (Karnataka) lies in the Western Ghats, next to Mudumalai and Wayanad.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
items.s: The Marine National Park is located in
items.x: India's first Marine National Park is in the Gulf of Kachchh, Gujarat (1982). Lakshadweep and Tamil Nadu have marine reserves, not this park.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: In which State is the Nokrek Biosphere reserve is located?
items.x: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve (Garo Hills) is in Meghalaya. Off-topic (protected areas), moved.

items.src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
items.s: In which of these states of India, Loktak lake is located?
items.x: Loktak Lake, the largest freshwater lake of the North-East and home of the floating Keibul Lamjao NP, is in Manipur.

items.s: From the following, choose the correct pair of Tiger Reserves and the states
items.x: Corbett Tiger Reserve (India's first, Project Tiger 1973) is in Uttarakhand. Buxa is in West Bengal, Bhadra in Karnataka, and Gir (Gujarat) is a lion national park, not a tiger reserve.

items.s: Which of the following tiger reserve lies in two States ?
items.x:
Most books and keys: Pench Tiger Reserve lies in two States (MP and Maharashtra). Strictly: there are two separate, adjoining tiger reserves named Pench, one in MP and one in Maharashtra, listed separately by NTCA (Shankar Environment 24 p.3; PMF Environment 03 p.91, joint TX2 Award 2023).
Pench is the answer: the Pench forests on the Pench river straddle Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. Kanha (MP), Manas (Assam; it adjoins Bhutan, not another State) and Sariska (Rajasthan) each lie in one State.

items.s: In which one of the following States is Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary located?
items.x: Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary, also the Pakke Tiger Reserve, is in East Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh, next to Nameri (Assam). It is not in Manipur, Meghalaya or Nagaland.

items.s:
Consider the following areas –
1. Bandipur
2. Bhitarkanika
3. Manas
4. Sunderbans
Which of the above are Tiger Reserves?
items.x: Bandipur (Karnataka), Manas (Assam) and Sunderbans (West Bengal) are tiger reserves. Bhitarkanika (Odisha) is a mangrove national park and sanctuary, not a tiger reserve; Odisha's tiger reserves are Similipal and Satkosia.

items.s: Which one of the following Tiger reserves of India is located in Mizoram?
items.x: Dampa Tiger Reserve is in western Mizoram. Melghat is in Maharashtra, Buxa in West Bengal and Bhadra in Karnataka.

items.src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
items.s: Which Indian state is known as the 'Falcon Capital of the world'?
items.x: Nagaland (Pangti, Doyang reservoir, Wokha) is called the 'Falcon Capital of the World' for its Amur falcon roost. Off-topic (wildlife), moved.

items.s: In which State is Valmiki Tiger Reserve located?
items.x: Valmiki is in Bihar; Nagarhole is in Karnataka and Ranthambore in Rajasthan.

items.s: In which hills does Periyar Tiger Reserve lie?
items.x: Periyar is in the Western Ghats; Nagarjunsagar–Srisailam is in the Nallamala Hills and Similipal in the Eastern Ghats.

items.s: Tadoba Tiger Reserve is associated with which landscape?
items.x: Tadoba lies in the Deccan and central Indian forest landscape of Maharashtra.

items.s: In which district of Maharashtra is the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve?
items.x: Tadoba-Andhari, one of the oldest tiger reserves, is in Chandrapur district.

items.s: Rajaji in Uttarakhand became India's tiger reserve of which number in 2015?
items.x: Rajaji became the 48th tiger reserve in 2015; Orang became the 49th.

items.s: Ravines are mostly found in India in the
items.x: India's ravines are concentrated in the Chambal–Yamuna basin on the southern fringe of the Gangetic plain (Chambal ravines of MP, Rajasthan, UP). Narmada valley and the Shivaliks (chos) have local gullies, but the bulk of ravine land lies on the periphery of the Ganga plain.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Which one of the following bacteria present in the soil produces a peculiar smell if it rains on parched soil?
items.x: The earthy smell of rain on dry soil (petrichor) comes from geosmin made by soil Streptomyces (actinomycetes); Micrococcus and the other names do not make it.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
items.s: Scientific study of soil is
items.x: Pedology is the scientific study of soils (formation, classification, mapping); edaphology studies soil in relation to plants.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
items.s: Eluviation of soils means
items.x: Eluviation is the mobilisation and downward washing out (translocation) of clay, iron and humus from an upper horizon; their deposit lower down is illuviation.

items.s: Which of the following soil predominates the Sundarban area?
items.x: The Sundarbans in the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta have (saline) deltaic alluvial soil, not red, laterite or black soil.

items.s: Which one of the following crop enriches the Nitrogen content in soil ?
items.x: Pea is a legume whose root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen and enrich the soil; potato, sorghum and sunflower do not.

items.s: Which one of the following crops is grown to improve the soil fertility ?
items.x: Black gram (urd) is a pulse that fixes nitrogen and improves soil fertility; wheat, rice and sugarcane deplete it.

items.s:
Given below are two statements, in which one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as
Reason (R) :
Assertion (A) : Saline soils in India are not appropriate for cultivation of crops.
Reason (R) : Saline soils have high proportion of salt, largely because of dry climate and poor drainage.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
items.x: Saline soils are unfit for crops because they hold too much salt, which builds up from a dry climate and poor drainage, so R explains A.

items.s: Halophytes grow well in –
items.x: Halophytes grow in saline soils; cryophytes grow in cold soils, lithophytes on rock and xerophytes in deserts.

items.src: Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fisheries
items.s: Out of the below, Which is the largest soil group in terms of area in India?
items.x: Alluvial soil is India's largest soil group (~45.6% of the area); laterite, desert and saline soils are much smaller.

items.s: Which of the following is devoted to study the processes of soil formation, soil types, their fertility status, distribution and use?
items.x: Soil geography studies soil formation, types, fertility, distribution and use; hydrology, climatology and geomorphology deal with water, climate and landforms.

items.s: Which of the following is concerned with soil?
items.x: Edaphic means relating to the soil (its physical and chemical make-up); climatic, biotic and topographic factors are different.

items.s: Soil water available to plants is maximum in :
items.x:
Most books and keys: clay soil. Strictly, plant-available water (field capacity minus wilting point) is highest in loamy / silt-loam soils, because clay holds much of its water too tightly for roots (general knowledge, not checked).
Exam keys answer clay soil, because clay holds the most water in its fine pores; see the dispute for plant-available water.

items.s: Capillaries are most effective in –
items.x: Capillary rise is strongest in clayey soil with the finest pores and weakest in sandy soil.

items.s: A fertile soil, suitable for growing common crops is likely to have a pH value of :
items.x: Most common crops grow best near neutral, pH 6 to 7; pH 3–4 is strongly acidic and 9–10 strongly alkaline.

items.s: In which of the following States is black soil predominantly found?
items.x: Black (regur) soil covers the largest area in Maharashtra, on the Deccan Trap basalt. Rajasthan, UP and Meghalaya have desert, alluvial and laterite or red soils.

items.src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Which of the following Indian State is having Laterite Soils?
items.x: Andhra Pradesh has laterite soils (Eastern Ghats/coastal uplands); UP, Punjab and Haryana are alluvial.

items.src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
items.s: The arid & desert soil is found in the states/regions of:
items.x: Arid (desert) soils occur in north-west India – western Rajasthan, Kutch/Gujarat and adjoining Haryana-Punjab; Maharashtra has black soils.

items.s: Where are diamond mines in India?
items.x: India's diamond mines are at Panna (and Satna) in Madhya Pradesh. Moved (Indian minerals).

items.src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
items.s: Cuddapah system is composed of
items.x: The Cuddapah system was formed by deposition of unfossiliferous clay, slates, sandstones and limestones in synclinal basins; gneiss belongs to the older Archaean basement. Off-topic (rock systems), moved.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
items.s: Coal deposits in India occur in
items.x: Nearly 98% of India's coal is in the Gondwana rocks; moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which Rock system in India has most of the coal reserves
items.x: Gondwana rocks hold nearly 98% of India's coal; Dharwar is metal-rich, Vindhyan gives building stone and Tertiary gives oil and lignite. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: In which rock system, out of the following, is iron-ore found in India ?
items.x: India's iron ore occurs mainly in the Dharwar system. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which one of the following rock systems in India is the main source of coal deposits?
items.x: The Gondwana system is the main source of India's coal (about 98–99%). Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: The most mineralized rock system of India is –
items.x: The Dharwar system is the most mineralised (iron ore, manganese, copper, lead, gold). Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which of the following geological systems of rocks contain a rich reserve of iron ore in India?
items.x: Rich iron ore reserves are in the Dharwar system. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which of the following rock systems provides over 90% of the coal of India?
items.x: The Gondwana system provides over 90% (nearly 98%) of India's coal. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which of the following rock systems is the major source of metallic minerals in India?
items.x: The Dharwar system is the major source of metallic minerals. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which of the following rock systems in India is the latest one?
items.x: Order: Dharwar → Cuddapah → Vindhyan → Gondwana, so Gondwana is the latest of the four. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which one of the following is the appropriate reason for considering the Gondwana rocks as most important of rock systems of India?
o: More than 90% of limestone reserves of India are
More than 90% of India's coal reserves are found in
More than 90% of fertile black cotton soils are spread
None of the reasons given above is appropriate in this
items.x: Gondwana rocks matter most because they hold over 90% of India's coal. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Kaimur Plateau is famous for :
items.x: The Kaimur Plateau (Vindhyan) is famous for limestone, the base of the cement industry (Banjari). Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: The Chota Nagpur Plateau is primarily composed of
o: Archean rocks of granite and gneiss
items.x: The Chota Nagpur Plateau is made mainly of Archaean granite and gneiss. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of geomorphic structures present in India, from oldest to the youngest?
items.x: Oldest to youngest: Dharwar → Cuddapah → Vindhyan → Gondwana. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: A huge amount of sources found in the Vindhya rocks are of –
items.x: The Vindhyan sedimentary rocks are rich in limestone (with sandstone, china clay) – base of the cement industry. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which of the following geographical series is NOT related to Vindhyan system?
items.x: Semri, Kaimur and Rewa are Vindhyan series; Khondalites are Archaean rocks of the Eastern Ghats. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Read the following statements and choose the correct option : Statement - I : J.D. Dana prepared a special Geological Time Scale to indicate the geological history of Indian subcontinent rocks Statement - II : As per Geological Time Scale, Indian rocks are subdivided into Archaean, Puranic, Dravidian and Aryan periods
o: Statement - I and Statement - II both are true
Statement -I and Statement - II both are false
Statement - I is true but Statement - II is false
Statement - I is false but Statement - II is true
items.x: Statement I is false – Sir T.H. Holland (GSI), not J.D. Dana, made the Indian scale; Statement II is true (Archaean, Purana, Dravidian, Aryan). Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.s: Which of the following has the oldest rock system in the country?
items.x: The Aravallis are made of the oldest (Archaean–Dharwar) rocks among the options; the Himalayas, Siwaliks and the Indo-Gangetic plain are young. Moved to the Indian rock systems row.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics 2017
items.s: The National Mineral Exploration Policy, 2016 contains one of the following?
o: Restriction of private participation in mining sector
Conservative approach in use of mineral resources
Allocation of extra amount of Rs. 10,000 Cr to GSI in five years
Making available baseline geo-scientific data of world standards in public domain
items.x: The National Mineral Exploration Policy 2016 makes pre-competitive baseline geoscientific data of world standard available in the public domain as a public good, and it invites private participation (auction of exploration blocks) – it does not restrict it.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forests General Studies & Men
items.s: As per Annual Report 2021-22 of the Ministry of Mines, production of gold ore in India decreased by ____ % in 2020-21, as compared to previous year.
items.x:
Printed key: 12.8% (Ministry of Mines Annual Report 2021-22, provisional data). The final Indian Minerals Yearbook 2021 shows a fall of about 24.3%.
The printed key (12.8%) is the Ministry of Mines Annual Report 2021-22 figure; it could not be opened. The final IBM data show gold ore falling from 595,511 t (2019-20) to 450,611 t (2020-21).

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: The percentage of total rare earth oxides in Monazite ore is generally around (choose nearest figure)?
items.x: Monazite usually carries about 55-60% total rare-earth oxides (besides thorium), so 60% is the nearest figure.

items.src: Assistant Director in AP Economics and Statistics 2017
items.s: Which of the States is the top bauxite producer in India?
items.x: Odisha (Orissa) is India's largest bauxite-producing state (Koraput, Kalahandi, Rayagada); Gujarat is second and Jharkhand third. Off-topic here: moved to Geography.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Which state is the largest producer of Copper in India?
items.x: Madhya Pradesh (Malanjkhand, Balaghat) is the leading copper producer, though Rajasthan has the largest reserves.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forests General Studies & Men
items.s: Barring some sporadic occurrences here and there in isolated pockets, minerals are generally concentrated in Three broad belts in India, which one of the following is NOT one of these belts?
items.x: NCERT's three mineral belts are the North-Eastern Plateau, the South-Western Plateau and the North-Western region; a 'South-Eastern Region' belt is not one of them.

items.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
items.s: Which State of the following is having lignite reserves along with Tamil Nadu State?
items.x: Besides Tamil Nadu (Neyveli), lignite reserves occur mainly in Rajasthan (Barmer, Bikaner) and Gujarat. Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh are not lignite States.

items.s: As per the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2021, ____ was the leading producer of primary gold accounting for 99% production in 2020-21.
items.x: Karnataka (Hutti mines) produced about 99% of India's primary gold in 2020-21 (IMYB 2021).

items.src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
items.s: What is the Indian name of Fuller's earth?
items.x: Fuller's earth is called Multani Mitti in India; milk of magnesia is magnesium hydroxide and sindhuram is vermilion.

items.s: What is the global rank of India in terms of Manganese ore production by the 2019? (As per reports of Ministry of mines, Govt. of India)
items.x: IBM's Indian Minerals Yearbook 2019 (Manganese Ore) ranks 2018 world output as South Africa 28%, China 17%, Australia 14%, Ghana 9%, Gabon 8%, Brazil 6%, then India 5%. So India was 7th.

items.s: Which of the following is NOT a reason for the occurrence of landslides?
items.x: Heavy rainfall, steep slopes and deforestation all trigger landslides. Plantations (tree cover) bind the soil, so they are not a cause.

items.src: APPSC Lecturers in Govt Degree Colleges Paper-I General Stud
items.s: Approximately what percent of India's landmass falls within Zone V, which is considered the most seismically active region?
items.x: Zone V (very high seismic risk) covered about 11% of India's area on the BIS seismic map (IS 1893:2002); Zone IV ~18%, Zone III ~30%.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-I Screening Test 2017
items.s: In which of the following places landslides are a frequent hazard?
items.x: Uttarakhand's young, steep Himalayan slopes and heavy monsoon rain make landslides a frequent hazard; Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha have far lower risk.

items.src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
items.s: Which Indian State is most vulnerable to cyclones?
items.x: Odisha, on the Bay of Bengal coast, is the state most vulnerable to cyclones among these; Rajasthan is inland.

items.s: Which State of India is most prone to cyclones?
items.x: Of the options, Andhra Pradesh on the Bay of Bengal coast is the most cyclone-prone (the east coast gets far more cyclones than Gujarat); Punjab and Rajasthan are inland.

items.s: Which state borders Telangana in the north?
items.x: Telangana borders Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh to the north; Odisha, Karnataka and Jharkhand do not lie on its northern side. Off-topic (political geography).

items.src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
items.s: Name the area wise largest district of Andhra Pradesh
items.at: YSR Kadapa (now; Anantapur before the 2022 reorganisation)
items.x:

items.s:
Statement: The geography of Andhra Pradesh has shaped its economic landscape in multiple ways:

1. The Eastern Ghats restricted inland trade routes.

2. The Krishna-Godavari deltas supported rice cultivation.

3. The Bay of Bengal coastline enabled maritime commerce.

4. The Rayalaseema region faced water scarcity challenges.

5. Visakhapatnam's port boosted colonial trade.
Question: Which of these factors most significantly contributed to Andhra Pradesh's historical economic prosperity?
items.x: Agrarian wealth from the Krishna-Godavari deltas (2), maritime commerce along the Bay of Bengal (3) and Visakhapatnam's port trade (5) drove prosperity. The Ghats' barrier (1) and Rayalaseema's water scarcity (4) were constraints.

items.s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT for the mineral Asbestos?

I. Asbestos is known for its heat resistance capacity

II. Andhra Pradesh is the leading producer of Asbestos in India
items.x:
Key: Only II. Strictly Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa chrysotile) was India's only asbestos-producing State until 2013-14, so II was true then; no production since 2014-15 (IMYB 2022 Asbestos; Lok Sabha reply cited in web search).
The key marks only II incorrect: asbestos resists heat (I true), but India now has no asbestos production and Rajasthan holds most resources.

items.s: Andhra Pradesh is the sole producer of which of the following minerals in India?
items.x:
Key: apatite. Strictly IMYB reports India's apatite production as nil since 2016-17, and AP's true sole-producer mineral is barytes (IMYB Apatite & Rock Phosphate reviews, web search).
The key is apatite: AP (Kasipatnam, Visakhapatnam) ranks first in apatite and was its producer; calcite, bauxite and dolomite come from several States.

items.s: Andhra Pradesh has largest deposits of which of the following mineral?
items.x:
No printed key. Two options fit: AP has ~96% of chrysotile asbestos (IMYB 2022) and also the largest uranium resources (1,44,541 t U3O8 in a 2017 government table, web search); chrysotile is keyed as the near-monopoly.
Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa) holds about 96% of India's chrysotile asbestos resources (7.98 of 8.32 lakh t). It also leads in uranium (Tummalapalle), but not in iron ore or marble.

items.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the predominant type of iron ore is which one of the following?

items.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Swarnagiri Gold Mine?
o: It was renamed from the Jonnagiri Gold Mine
It is an underground mine operated under a ten-year lease
It belongs to the Jonnagiri greenstone belt
It is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district

Asbestos production and reserves are highest in Kadapa.

items.s: By what name is Andhra Pradesh often called because of its rich and varied mineral deposits?

items.s: Pulivendula in Andhra Pradesh is known for deposits of which mineral?
items.x: Pulivendula in Kadapa district has asbestos; Kadapa ranks first in AP for asbestos.
